summary: Contestants apply managerial accounting principles to analyze costs, prepare budgets, and use advanced costing methods and analytics to support pricing, performance evaluation, and strategic decision-making. The event consists of an objective and application test, and is open to postsecondary students. Contestants must bring specified materials and follow event rules during the timed competition.
time_limits: no more than ten (10) minutes for orientation
no more than ninety (90) minutes for testing
no more than ten (10) minutes for wrap-up
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non -electronic written reference materials
Cordless calculator: Electronic devices will be monitored according to ACT standards.  See NLC Calculator Guidelines. Contestants who violate this rule will be disqualified.
competencies: Differentiate between managerial and financial accounting
Define materials, labor, factory overhead, and sustainability -related costs and apply advanced overhead allocation methods
Prepare entries for Job Order and Process Costing Systems
Calculate product cost using activity -based costing integrated with data analytics
Classify costs by behavior and analyze cost patterns
Calculate break -even and target profit incorporating dynamic pricing models
Prepare variable and absorption costing income statements
Describe and prepare the basic types of budgets
Describe standard costing and variances with real -time data tracking
Calculate price, labor, and overhead variances
Describe responsibility accounting and integrate with performance dashboards
Use differential analysis and predictive analytics to make data -driven decisions
Determine selling price, total cost, and product cost using variable cost concepts
Explain capital investment analysis using discounted cash flow and scenario modeling
eligibility_notes: Any postsecondary student contestant may enter this application event.
